title: Television Channels

Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Reality shows are a type of ______ programme. (ii) Television programmes are broadly classified into ______ categories.
Fill in the blanks: ______ and ______ are nature and science related channels.
Match: (i) Cartoon Network (ii) ESPN (iii) Discovery (iv) NDTV 24x7 with (a) science (b) sports (c) children (d) news.
State true or false: (i) Comedy shows are entertainment programmes. (ii) Culture and gender studies programmes are informative.
Name two special audience programmes on television.
questions.answer: Children's programmes and women's programmes (also youth and farmers').

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Name any two categories of television channels with an example of each.
questions.answer: News channels – Aaj Tak; sports channels – ESPN (also cartoon – Pogo).

questions.q: What are infotainment and edutainment?
questions.answer: New words for programmes that combine information or education with entertainment, in which entertainment is common.

questions.q: What is a soap opera?
questions.answer: A continuing episodic dramatic serial; the name comes from radio serials sponsored by soap makers.

questions.q: Give two examples of educational programmes.
questions.answer: Open university and distance learning (UGC, IGNOU) programmes and health, agriculture or literacy campaigns; Gyandarshan.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Discuss three types of informative television programmes with examples.
questions.answer: News and current affairs (bulletins, panel discussions); sports programmes (cricket matches, sports diaries); cookery and food shows (Khana Khazana); also science and environment programmes (Surabhi).

questions.q: Describe the categories of television channels.
questions.answer: News, sports, cartoon, entertainment and lifestyle, and science and discovery channels, each for a different audience.

questions.q: Explain the types of entertainment programmes with examples.
questions.answer: Serials and soaps, comedy shows, musical programmes, game and chat shows, cartoons, fairy tales, horror and reality shows like Indian Idol.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Differentiate between fiction and non-fiction television programme formats with examples in each category.
questions.answer: Fiction is imaginative and dramatized for entertainment (serials such as Ghar Ek Mandir, soap operas, film-based programmes); non-fiction is based on real events and information (news bulletins, quiz shows like Bournvita Quiz Contest, talks and discussions like We the People).

questions.q: Discuss the various categories of television channels in detail, giving examples.
questions.answer: News (Aaj Tak, NDTV 24x7), sports (ESPN), cartoon (Pogo, Cartoon Network), entertainment and lifestyle (Zoom) and science and discovery (National Geographic, Discovery) channels.
